end_state: By episode 100 Bellwether has a publicly auditable flood registry, the erased residents have recovered legal identities, and Iona has learned Tomas's fate without undoing the losses or sacrificing witness consent.
intentions: Iona finds Tomas Vale's name in an evacuation ledger and a brass token numbered 47; she hides the token while leaving the ledger in the archive.
Iona asks Sef Marr about token 47; his stiff left hand complicates handling it, and he makes her promise not to identify him to the council.
Neri Pell independently detects a survey discrepancy at Gate Nine; Iona shares the token number but withholds Tomas's name and Sef's involvement.
At Gate Nine Iona and Neri hear three short bell strokes and recover a page stitched with blue thread, distinguishing bell signal from token identifier.
Iona shows Sef the recovered page; he recognises an evacuation route, and the three allies secure a copy while the original goes into Iona's sealed tin.
Iona authenticates the blue-thread page against a public tide record without revealing Sef; Neri still does not know Tomas's connection.
A council inspector asks Iona for the page; she refuses to surrender her sealed original and learns the new sea wall's evidence-destroying timetable.
Neri catches Iona concealing a personal stake; Iona voluntarily tells her Tomas is her brother while preserving Sef's identity from the council.
With informed consent Sef describes a clerical transfer that erased residents; his testimony implicates a process, not proof of Ada Rusk's guilt.
The allies test the transfer against one consenting living resident's records, prove an identity was erased, and choose a safe next witness without learning Tomas's fate.
The erased resident Leda Moss explains how loss of registration barred her from work.
Iona helps Leda obtain a temporary identity receipt without exposing her testimony.
Neri maps the old route against the planned foundations and identifies a threatened chamber.
Sef supplies a key with a documented chain of custody rather than a promise of answers.
The allies enter the chamber during a lawful inspection window and find numbered intake tags.
Iona records the tags in place and discovers that number 47 has a missing counterpart.
A contractor disputes their access and Iona negotiates a witnessed return visit.
Leda introduces another erased resident who refuses publicity but permits anonymised corroboration.
The records show erasure preceded the current sea wall proposal.
Iona decides to seek independent archival verification before accusing any official.
Archivist Oren Venn agrees to examine copies under a written confidentiality condition.
Oren separates original entries from later insertions using paper and ink evidence.
Neri locates the supplier of the blue binding thread.
The supplier's surviving invoices link the thread to a municipal annex.
Iona applies for annex access and receives a narrow refusal with appeal instructions.
Ada Rusk offers a private meeting and Iona brings a witness.
Ada admits the timetable is political but denies knowing about erased residents.
An appeal grants access to indexes but not personal files.
The index reveals Tomas's file moved twice after his disappearance.
Iona chooses to follow transfer receipts rather than steal a restricted file.
A former courier identifies the first transfer destination as a quarantine hostel.
The hostel custodian allows inspection of nonpersonal maintenance records.
Three short bell strokes are confirmed as a historic evacuation clearance signal.
Neri reconstructs how the signal and route could conceal unauthorised transfers.
Sef admits he once rang the clearance bell without seeing every passenger.
Iona struggles with his omission but distinguishes complicity from what he could know.
A survivor describes the hostel's conditions and declines to discuss Tomas.
The group creates a consent register for testimonies and withdrawals.
An unsigned warning names a current clerk who handled the second transfer.
Iona protects that clerk from public accusation while requesting an interview.
Clerk Hessa Dorn agrees to speak with independent counsel present.
Hessa explains a registry consolidation instruction that made people administratively absent.
Oren identifies who signed the instruction and who merely executed it.
Ada's predecessor emerges as an author of the policy, without clearing Ada's present conduct.
Neri finds the sea wall survey reused the erased population's empty-house designation.
Leda confronts the difference between physical occupancy and official vacancy.
Iona files a narrow request to suspend demolition of occupied properties.
A hearing demands named claimants and threatens witness privacy.
The allies develop a sealed submission process with legal assistance.
The hearing grants a temporary pause but excludes the submerged evidence chamber.
A spring tide damages the chamber and forces a documented salvage operation.
Iona prioritises witnesses' safety over retrieving a potentially decisive box.
Sef supervises the gate procedure within his physical limitations.
Neri recovers a register fragment and logs its damaged condition.
Oren refuses to infer missing names from the fragment's torn edge.
A surviving receipt places Tomas at a mainland transfer station seven years ago.
Iona asks a mainland archivist for an authorised search.
The search returns two men with similar names and Iona rejects premature identification.
Leda's reopened record generates resistance from the registry office.
The allies win one correction that establishes a precedent rather than a universal cure.
Ada proposes compensation without admitting registry wrongdoing.
Residents debate immediate relief versus a full public record.
Iona refuses to speak for residents who have not authorised her.
Hessa supplies evidence that current officials received warnings about erroneous vacancy data.
Ada's office acknowledges receipt but disputes the warning's meaning.
An independent engineer links the bad data to unsafe evacuation planning.
Neri presents a corrected population map with uncertainty marked.
A storm forecast forces the city to act before the political dispute is resolved.
Sef and residents organise a transparent evacuation rehearsal.
The rehearsal reveals a gate bottleneck that the official plan overlooked.
The city repairs the bottleneck and publicly credits residents' evidence.
A mainland record confirms Tomas survived the original transfer.
Iona learns Tomas later used another legal name and requests contact through an intermediary.
The intermediary reports Tomas is alive but needs time before responding.
Iona honours his boundary while the registry investigation continues.
Oren assembles a chronology separating established facts from unresolved allegations.
Ada contests one date and supplies a document that corrects the chronology.
The correction strengthens the report's credibility despite embarrassing the allies.
Hessa agrees to testify publicly within her stated consent limits.
The commission opens with residents' legal injuries rather than Iona's family story.
Sef testifies about the bell and acknowledges his own limited responsibility.
Neri demonstrates the map discrepancy using reproducible measurements.
Leda describes the consequences of being absent from the registry.
The commission identifies the policy's authors and its current perpetuators separately.
Ada admits delaying investigation to protect the sea wall timetable.
A contractor produces records revealing who benefited from empty-house classifications.
The commission recommends restitution and independent registry oversight.
Tomas consents to a private meeting with Iona away from the hearings.
Tomas explains his survival and later silence without providing a simple reconciliation.
Iona accepts that restoring a name cannot restore the lost seven years.
Residents choose representatives to oversee implementation of the recommendations.
Neri designs a public map that protects private testimony locations.
Sef helps train new lockkeepers with a written clearance procedure.
Iona returns the brass token to a consent-based civic archive with its provenance intact.
Leda obtains a permanent corrected identity and challenges a remaining employment barrier.
The sea wall resumes under a revised plan that includes formerly erased residents.
A disputed registry entry tests whether the new appeals process works without Iona's intervention.
The appeal succeeds and Iona chooses a life beyond guarding every record herself.
Iona and Tomas make a modest future arrangement while acknowledging their changed relationship.
Bellwether opens its auditable flood registry; Iona watches three recorded bell strokes announce an evacuation drill with no person omitted.
purpose: Follow Iona from an isolated clerk to the organiser of a public evidentiary reckoning, with ten escalating ten-episode movements; the first two five-episode arcs are evidence acquisition and authentication.
